content.text: All fallback elements — and nearly all preferred elements — are satisfied in § 21, with no offsetting one-sided cap elsewhere (§ 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liability, and § 20 imposes no cap on indemnities).

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 meets our preferred position on its material terms, so it sits above the fallback and we do not redline it. § 21.1 imposes an expressly mutual aggregate cap at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000; § 21.2 excludes indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive and consequential damages mutually (and helpfully confirms data-restoration, replacement-service, notice and incident-response costs are direct damages); § 21.3 places confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP outside the cap as Excluded Claims. "Fees" (§ 1.5) is a substantive revenue measure (recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees), so the cap basis is not illusory. Two minor points noted but not flagged: the payment carve-out in § 21.3 is limited to "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" rather than all amounts due — a narrowing that runs in our favour — and taxes/expenses/implementation charges are excluded from the Fees measure, which is a standard drafting nuance rather than a fallback failure. No hidden one-sided cap exists: § 20 leaves indemnities uncapped and § 18.2 states insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.
